entries.test: Enterprise deployment studies, documented workflow changes, and employment records could establish whether generative AI works in production and replaces workers at scale.
entries.note: He later explicitly qualifies worker replacement as replacement at scale and acknowledges effects on contract workers. The proposition omits that qualification.

entries.test: Published enterprise evaluations and user surveys could show whether the tools deliver their intended workflow functions and whether users recognize failures.
entries.note: The supplied condition appropriately restricts this to the enterprise tools under discussion.
The $600 billion forecast is explicitly qualified by 'likely.' The retrospective $500 billion assertion is independently checkable.

entries.test: Bankruptcy filings and financial reporting following an AI investment collapse would show whether the major GPU buyers mostly remain solvent.
entries.note: 'For the most part' limits the proportion of companies, rather than expressing a probability.

entries.test: Public inventory reports, GPU utilization data, and reporting on unused hardware could establish whether substantial GPU stocks sit warehoused for lack of applications.
entries.note: The warehousing prediction has a concrete reading despite the surrounding rhetoric. The accompanying counterfactual is not independently testable.

entries.test: Historical application inference spending and token-consumption data through publication could establish whether inference costs had fallen or were trending downward.
entries.note: The tentative future possibility does not hedge the firm claim about the existing cost trend. His surrounding discussion concerns application costs, not simply token prices.
Ranking the necessity of generative AI against urban taxis is a judgment of relative worth. The narrower assertion about substitute products is independently checkable.
'Maybe' qualifies the revenue figure. The separate assertion that these companies produce no profit is firm and independently checkable.
'A good chance' explicitly makes this a probabilistic assertion.

entries.test: A publicly documented, independently reproducible LLM demonstration of learning from new experience and revising its conclusions would falsify the claim.
entries.note: The categorical 'never' prediction has no deadline. Its present-tense component can also be assessed against existing demonstrations.
The central assertion attributes a private motive to OpenAI's reporting choice. Comparing weekly and monthly user totals would not establish that motive.

entries.test: Published training compute and performance comparisons, together with infrastructure cost and capability data, could test diminishing training returns and whether OpenAI's infrastructure provides advantages beyond serving scale.
entries.note: He makes a firm causal claim, including the restrictive assertion 'nothing more.'

entries.test: OpenAI's published paid-subscriber and active-user figures over the months following August 2025 would show whether its conversion rate materially improved.
entries.note: The conversion-rate prediction is firm despite the separate expression of disbelief about perpetual growth. More than a year has elapsed, allowing assessment of its ordinary near-term reading.
'Things' looking like they are 'collapsing' supplies no shared outcome or measure. He expressly declines to predict a bubble bursting.
